FR-001.title: Phase 1 MUST replace player-accessible hacking cheats with server-authoritative Fallout-style special patterns.

FR-002.title: The player experience MUST expose no command, board entry, protocol operation, browser global, DOM control, keyboard shortcut, or query parameter that directly forces puzzle success.

FR-003.title: The player experience MUST remove the former administrator shortcut that bulk-removes incorrect passwords.

FR-004.title: Ordinary candidate-word guesses and filler clicks MUST retain their existing password-match, likeness, attempt-spending, logging, success, and failure rules.

FR-005.title: The existing game-master `ForceHackSuccess` control MUST remain available only through the private desktop/Wails boundary.

FR-006.title: `ForceHackSuccess` MUST NOT be exposed through the player WebSocket protocol, browser globals, DOM controls, keyboard shortcuts, or query parameters.

FR-007.title: A successful trusted `ForceHackSuccess` action MUST use the existing shared success flow without consuming an attempt.

FR-008.title: A valid special pattern MUST use exactly one matching delimiter type from `()`, `[]`, `{}`, or `<>`.

FR-009.title: A valid special pattern MUST start and end on the same rendered row.

FR-010.title: A valid special pattern MUST contain no alphabetic character between its endpoints.

FR-011.title: Pattern discovery MUST pair each opening delimiter with the first compatible closing delimiter to its right on the same rendered row.

FR-012.title: A discovered pattern MUST be represented by an inclusive opening-through-closing coordinate range.

FR-013.title: Multiple opening delimiters that share the same first compatible closing delimiter MUST be discovered as distinct patterns.

FR-014.title: Using one pattern MUST NOT consume another pattern with a different complete coordinate pair.

FR-015.title: Before publication, a newly generated puzzle board MUST contain between three and six distinct selectable special patterns inclusive.

FR-016.title: The initial pattern count MUST be computed from the final rendered board using the same discovery algorithm used during gameplay.

FR-017.title: A final rendered board with fewer than three or more than six discovered patterns MUST be regenerated before publication.

FR-018.title: The initial three-to-six limit MUST apply only until the first player action.

FR-019.title: Gameplay discovery after board mutation MUST publish all current valid patterns even when their count exceeds six.

FR-020.title: The initial three-to-six limit MUST NOT vary by hacking difficulty.

FR-021.title: A special-pattern identity MUST contain the puzzle generation identifier, rendered row, opening-character index, and closing-character index.

FR-022.title: Pattern used state MUST belong to the complete generation-and-coordinate identity.

FR-023.title: A complete pattern identity MUST be accepted at most once during its puzzle generation.

FR-024.title: When board mutation causes the same opening character to pair with a different first compatible closing character, the resulting coordinate pair MUST be treated as a new pattern identity.

FR-025.title: A coordinate pair already used in the active puzzle generation MUST remain unavailable if that pair is later rediscovered.

FR-026.title: Replacing a removed incorrect password with periods MUST trigger discovery against the resulting canonical rendered board.

FR-027.title: Each accepted pattern activation MUST independently select one outcome using server-side weighted randomness.

FR-028.title: Eighty percent of the random-source value space MUST map to dud removal.

FR-029.title: Twenty percent of the random-source value space MUST map to attempt restoration.

FR-030.title: A dud-removal outcome MUST remove exactly one currently available incorrect password candidate.

FR-031.title: Dud removal MUST replace the selected incorrect password with periods without altering the correct password.

FR-032.title: An attempt-restoration outcome MUST set remaining attempts to the configured maximum without exceeding it.

FR-033.title: A selected dud-removal outcome MUST apply attempt restoration instead when no removable incorrect password remains.

FR-034.title: Invalid, stale, already-used, or otherwise rejected pattern requests MUST NOT consume a random-source value.

FR-035.title: Verification MUST use an injected deterministic random source for outcome mapping and activation-order tests.

FR-036.title: A controlled source spanning 100 equiprobable values MUST map exactly 80 values to dud removal and 20 values to attempt restoration.

FR-037.title: Production behavior MUST be judged by the configured probability mapping rather than by requiring every sample of 100 accepted activations to contain exactly 80 dud removals and 20 restorations.

FR-038.title: Every `HACK_PATTERN` request MUST identify both the target pattern and the puzzle generation from which the client received it.

FR-039.title: A pattern target MUST be represented either by an opaque server-issued `patternId` that resolves to generation and coordinates or by an explicit equivalent containing only `generationId`, `row`, `start`, and `end`.

FR-040.title: The server MUST reject a `HACK_PATTERN` payload containing missing, unknown, or invalid fields.

FR-041.title: The server MUST reject a `HACK_PATTERN` request whose generation does not match the active puzzle generation.

FR-042.title: The server MUST reject coordinates that do not identify a currently valid pattern in canonical board state.

FR-043.title: The server MUST reject a pattern identity already marked used.

FR-044.title: The server MUST reject a pattern request when the puzzle is not in an actionable state.

FR-045.title: A request from an older generation MUST NOT activate a pattern at matching coordinates in a newer generation.

FR-046.title: Accepted pattern activation MUST execute under the canonical live-service mutex.

FR-047.title: Under that mutex, activation MUST perform these steps in order: validate the active generation; validate or rediscover the requested coordinate pair against canonical board state; verify unused state; mark the pair used; select the weighted outcome; apply the outcome or fallback; recompute patterns affected by mutation; produce a detached public projection; broadcast resulting canonical state.

FR-048.title: Concurrent requests for the same pattern MUST result in exactly one accepted activation.

FR-049.title: Rejected duplicate requests MUST NOT mutate canonical state.

FR-050.title: Rejected duplicate requests MUST NOT advance the random source.

FR-051.title: Player authorization MUST remain behind a distinct player/live-service boundary so a future active-session check can be added without changing hacking domain logic.

FR-052.title: Phase 1 MUST NOT implement an active controlling-player or observer authorization model.

FR-053.title: The public pattern projection MUST contain only a stable public pattern identity, rendered row, inclusive start and end coordinates, and current available-or-used status.

FR-054.title: The public pattern projection MUST contain the rendered row and inclusive start and end coordinates.

FR-055.title: The public pattern projection MUST state whether each pattern is currently available or used.

FR-056.title: The public pattern projection MUST NOT reveal the password, dud identities, future effects of unused patterns, or private candidate metadata.

FR-057.title: Every public projection MUST be detached from canonical slices, maps, and objects.

FR-058.title: Mutating a returned projection MUST NOT alter canonical state.

FR-059.title: Pattern availability, used identities, removed duds, remaining attempts, and pattern outcomes MUST remain runtime-only state.

FR-060.title: A reconnecting client MUST receive the current canonical puzzle state while the originating server process retains that puzzle.

FR-061.title: Phase 1 MUST NOT preserve an active puzzle across server application restarts.

FR-062.title: Phase 1 MUST NOT modify the version-1 persisted session schema.

FR-063.title: Every initially published board MUST interleave candidate password words, ordinary punctuation and filler symbols, delimiters belonging to valid special patterns, and standalone delimiter-decoy characters outside every currently valid pattern's inclusive interaction range.

FR-064.title: The generator MUST NOT reserve or group board rows or contiguous board regions by content type for candidate words, ordinary filler, valid patterns, or delimiter decoys.

FR-065.title: Production discovery MUST accept a matching same-row pattern with one or more ordinary non-alphabetic filler characters between its opening and first compatible closing delimiter.

FR-066.title: Every initially published board MUST contain at least one valid special pattern with one or more non-alphabetic filler characters between its endpoints.

FR-067.title: Production discovery MUST continue to accept an adjacent empty matching delimiter pair that satisfies all normal special-pattern rules.

FR-068.title: The generator MUST NOT construct every initial valid pattern as an adjacent empty pair.

FR-069.title: Matching delimiters surrounding a candidate word or other alphabetic content MUST NOT form a valid special pattern while that alphabetic content remains rendered.

FR-070.title: A candidate word inside an alphabetic-interrupted delimiter span MUST remain selectable under the existing candidate-word guess rules.
tests: tests/browser/hacking-camouflage.spec.mjs::word-interrupted spans stay ordinary until a server snapshot publishes a new pattern

FR-071.title: When dud removal replaces an incorrect word inside a delimiter span with periods, production discovery MUST publish the resulting span if it satisfies every normal special-pattern rule on the mutated board.
tests: tests/browser/hacking-camouflage.spec.mjs::word-interrupted spans stay ordinary until a server snapshot publishes a new pattern

FR-072.title: Every initially published board MUST contain standalone delimiter-decoy characters that are not part of any currently valid pattern interaction range.

FR-073.title: The number of standalone delimiter-decoy characters on every initially published board MUST be at least the number of initially valid special patterns.

FR-074.title: Every initially published board MUST contain at least one potential matching-delimiter span that is invalid because alphabetic content appears between its endpoints.

FR-075.title: A standalone delimiter decoy MUST NOT highlight, produce a HACK_PATTERN request, consume an attempt, or change puzzle state.
tests: tests/browser/hacking-camouflage.spec.mjs::valid patterns interact while standalone delimiters remain inert and visually identical

FR-076.title: A delimiter decoy MUST use the same color, brightness, font, CRT effect, and static styling as the same delimiter character when it belongs to a valid pattern.
tests: tests/browser/hacking-camouflage.spec.mjs::valid patterns interact while standalone delimiters remain inert and visually identical

FR-077.title: Pattern validity MUST be revealed only through normal hover, focus, or selection behavior for currently valid patterns.
tests: tests/browser/hacking-camouflage.spec.mjs::valid patterns interact while standalone delimiters remain inert and visually identical

FR-078.title: Candidate words and all camouflage characters MUST be added before initial-board validation begins.

FR-079.title: Initial-board validation MUST run the production discovery algorithm against the complete final rendered board and count every accidentally formed valid pattern toward the initial 3–6 limit.

FR-080.title: Initial-board validation MUST regenerate a board that fails the 3–6 valid-pattern limit, standalone delimiter-decoy minimum, non-empty valid-interior requirement, alphabetic-interrupted-span requirement, or mixed-distribution requirement.

FR-081.title: The public pattern projection MUST include only spans that are currently valid under production discovery.

FR-082.title: Standalone, mismatched, word-interrupted, later-compatible-but-unselected, and otherwise invalid delimiters MUST receive no public pattern identity.

FR-083.title: Camouflage construction and final-board validation MUST preserve the discovery rules in FR-008 through FR-013 unchanged.

SC-003.title: Across 1,000 generated and publishable initial boards, every complete board satisfies all pattern, camouflage, exact occupied-row distribution, and valid-only projection gates.

SC-004.title: Every generated board that fails any initial pattern-count or camouflage condition is rejected and regenerated after complete-board analysis.

SC-014.title: Controlled generator tests preserve adjacent empty pairs while preventing all-empty initial pattern sets.

SC-015.title: Executable browser interaction tests prove delimiter decoys are inert while valid patterns retain inclusive interaction behavior.

SC-016.title: Dynamic-board tests prove word-interrupted spans gain identity only after dud removal makes them valid.

SC-017.title: Static and computed-style checks find no persistent validity-dependent delimiter treatment.

decisions.decision: Replace HACK_ADMIN and the SUCCESS entry with HACK_PATTERN while retaining ForceHackSuccess
decisions.why: Separates the untrusted player mechanic from the trusted game-master override
decisions.rejected: Reusing the administrator message or removing the GM override

decisions.decision: Identify patterns by column, opening index, and closing index and rediscover them from current board text
decisions.why: Coordinates distinguish stacked patterns and support dynamic discovery without exposing secrets
decisions.rejected: Text identities, client-trusted coordinates, or generation-only random IDs

decisions.decision: Construct and verify exactly 3-6 isolated initial patterns using bracket-free ordinary filler
decisions.why: Guarantees the required count at every difficulty without incidental bracket interactions
decisions.rejected: Retrying uncontrolled random boards or publishing only a subset

decisions.decision: Validate, consume, resolve, and project each pattern activation under the existing live-service mutex
decisions.why: Makes simultaneous use produce at most one effect and one complete shared snapshot
decisions.rejected: Transport-layer deduplication or client-local disabling

decisions.decision: Use Intn(100) buckets 0-79 for dud removal and 80-99 for attempt restoration
decisions.why: Implements the exact 80/20 split through the existing deterministic random seam
decisions.rejected: Floating-point probability or a no-op dud fallback

decisions.decision: Drive range highlighting and activation from the public patterns projection
decisions.why: Supports overlapping spans while keeping canonical availability on the server
decisions.rejected: Independent JavaScript discovery or overlapping DOM wrappers

decisions.decision: Extend HACK_STATE and TERMINAL_LIVE additively with patterns and reject removed HACK_ADMIN input
decisions.why: Reuses existing convergence and reconnect envelopes while ensuring stale clients cannot retain the cheat
decisions.rejected: A new protocol version or a separate pattern snapshot message

decisions.decision: Seed each generated special pattern as an isolated adjacent bracket pair
decisions.why: A two-cell span is valid under the contract and guarantees the exact count without cross-pair interactions while the scanner still supports longer dynamic and stacked spans
decisions.rejected: Variable-length generated spans that can accidentally create extra compatible pairs

decisions.decision: Supersede coordinate-only pattern IDs with an opaque ID over generationId + row + inclusive start + inclusive end
decisions.why: Prevents stale cross-generation activation while preserving the existing HACK_PATTERN shape
decisions.rejected: Column/opening/closing-only IDs or a wider explicit request payload

decisions.decision: Use a flattened canonical rendered-row ordinal with row-local inclusive offsets
decisions.why: Meets the minimal public projection without exposing column or pair
decisions.rejected: Public column metadata or cross-column 24-character rows

decisions.decision: Issue puzzle generation IDs from a source independent of gameplay Random
decisions.why: Stale-request safety must not consume or perturb the deterministic outcome sequence
decisions.rejected: Restarting counters or drawing IDs from outcome randomness

decisions.decision: Regenerate until production discovery on the final rendered board reports 3-6 patterns
decisions.why: Final discovery is authoritative; intended insertion count is only a construction aid
decisions.rejected: Trusting inserted pairs, exact random target equality, or publishing a subset

decisions.decision: Consume one Intn(100) outcome value for every accepted activation before applying the no-dud fallback
decisions.why: Implements the mandated 80/20 mapping and activation order
decisions.rejected: Checking dud availability before the weighted selection

decisions.decision: Commit one detached publication callback as step nine while the live mutex is held
decisions.why: Preserves canonical mutation and broadcast ordering without moving WebSocket ownership into live state
decisions.rejected: Post-unlock broadcast races or direct network writes from the live package

decisions.decision: Project only id, row, inclusive start/end, and used for current spans while retaining complete used history privately
decisions.why: Provides rendering data without leaks and keeps rediscovered pairs unavailable
decisions.rejected: Public column/pair metadata or forgetting hidden used identities

decisions.decision: Use opaque server-issued pattern IDs derived from generation and inclusive rendered-row coordinates.
decisions.why: Prevents delayed old-puzzle requests from activating coincident coordinates while keeping private metadata off the wire.
decisions.rejected: Client-reconstructed or coordinate-only IDs.

decisions.decision: Issue generation IDs from an independent cryptographic runtime source and reserve gameplay RNG for board and outcome choices.
decisions.why: Stale identity safety must not perturb deterministic gameplay RNG tests or persisted schema.
decisions.rejected: Deriving generation identity from gameplay RNG or persisted puzzle seeds.

decisions.decision: Publish accepted pattern state through a non-reentrant callback while the live-service mutex still owns the transition.
decisions.why: Preserves the mandated validate-mark-draw-mutate-project-broadcast order and guarantees one publication for one acceptance.
decisions.rejected: Returning state and broadcasting after releasing the live mutex.

decisions.decision: Resolve exact pattern openings first, then choose the containing pattern with the nearest opening for other in-range cells
decisions.why: This enables inclusive interaction without making stacked patterns with shared closers unreachable from their distinct openings
decisions.rejected: Selecting the first containing range, which would mask nested pattern openings

decisions.decision: Amend the completed full-pipeline feature in place and preserve its oversized classification; implement the amendment through unchecked T049-T053.
Define mixed distribution by per-category occupied-row counts and pairwise-overlapping inclusive row intervals.
Use an isolated, exactly pinned and locked executable browser-test dependency because Go asset checks cannot execute DOM interaction or message dispatch.
Derive all camouflage categories only after unchanged production discovery analyzes the complete rendered board
decisions.why: Accidental spans and decoy membership are final-board properties and must share the gameplay validity authority
decisions.rejected: Trust construction-time intended pattern and decoy metadata

decisions.decision: Reject non-ASCII-alphabetic injected candidate placeholders and supplement from the built-in word bank
decisions.why: Published word-interrupted spans must contain alphabetic candidate content and scanner semantics are ASCII alphabetic
decisions.rejected: Count numeric placeholder content as alphabetic interruption
